learningObjectives: Define what Templates are and why we use them.
Create a Template from an existing TestCase.

elements.text: Independent example: four selected size combinations share an automated flow. A Template models that flow and linked data supplies its variations; generate concrete tests through a TemplateInstance.

Designing cars: some are blue, some black, some silver; some manual, some automatic. It would be wasteful to design every variant from scratch. Instead, you design ONE base car (the blueprint) and spin off variations from it. A Template is exactly this blueprint — a base TestCase that spins off into a series of similar TestCases, each with a slightly different test focus.

elements.description: Centralize the common flow in the Template. Existing generated tests need reinstantiation to reflect later model/data edits; merely editing the Template does not update every generated case. Review manual changes before regeneration.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Converting a TestCase into a Template

elements.text: Use the independent size-data example from the preceding lesson. Reusable block references are supported in Templates; resolving all references is not a universal conversion prerequisite.

elements.title: Prepare and convert
items: Review shared block references and decide whether a local variation is needed.
For a deliberate local variation, select that block reference and Resolve Reference; Module/configuration dependencies remain.
Select the TestCase and Convert to Template.
Link the intended data source, check paths and instantiate. Convert to TestCase is available, but loses template information.

elements.text: Preserve a recoverable copy before changing model structure. Do not assume that saving defines a universal Undo boundary.

Build a small hypothetical login flow with synthetic data, convert it to a Template and plan its data references. Original Academy exercise instructions and source workspaces were inaccessible; this local task is independent practice.

examPitfalls.title: Generated tests require regeneration
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Editing the model and assuming previously generated cases immediately change.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Review the impact and reinstantiate the linked TemplateInstance.

examPitfalls.title: Shared references are supported
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Resolving every Library block as an unconditional preparation step.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Keep deliberate reuse; resolve a specific reference only when local customization is required.

examPitfalls.title: Converting back loses information
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating Convert to TestCase as a harmless preview toggle.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Preserve template information before reverting the object type.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why use a Template instead of creating 4 individual TestCases for the shirt-size scenario?

options.text: Tosca does not allow creating more than 1 TestCase manually.
A Template models the shared flow and generates the four selected combinations through a TemplateInstance; later changes require regeneration.
Templates run faster than TestCases during execution.
Templates remove the need for a TestSheet entirely.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think of the car-design analogy — one blueprint, many variations.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Model and data centralize maintenance; existing generated tests are refreshed through reinstantiation.

optionExplanations.A: Multiple manual TestCases are allowed; this is not the reason for templates.
optionExplanations.B: One flow model and chosen data combinations centralize generation and maintenance.
optionExplanations.C: A model is not an execution-speed guarantee.
optionExplanations.D: The scenario uses a TestSheet data source rather than eliminating it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Before converting a TestCase to a Template, what should you check?

options.text: Nothing — Templates can always be converted directly with no preparation.
Whether shared references should remain reusable or need deliberate local customization.
Whether an ExecutionList already exists.
Whether the TestSheet already has 100 Instances.

practiceQuiz.hint: This step also appeared in AS1 when editing shared Library content.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Templates support reusable block references. Resolve a particular reference when a local editable copy is intended, rather than as a universal conversion rule.

optionExplanations.A: Preparation includes intentional reuse and mapping decisions.
optionExplanations.B: Choose between shared reuse and a deliberate local editable block copy.
optionExplanations.C: An existing ExecutionList is not a conversion prerequisite.
optionExplanations.D: A fixed count of 100 Instances is not required.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How do you convert a ready TestCase into a Template?

options.text: Right-click the TestSheet → Convert to Template.
Rename the TestCase to start with 'Template_'.
Right-click the TestCase → Convert to Template.
Drag the TestCase onto the TestSheet.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a single right-click action on the TestCase itself.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Convert to Template acts on the selected TestCase and changes its object type; naming alone does not convert it.

optionExplanations.A: A TestSheet is a data-design object, not the TestCase being converted.
optionExplanations.B: Renaming does not change the object type.
optionExplanations.C: This context command converts the selected TestCase.
optionExplanations.D: Dropping a case onto a sheet is not this conversion command.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What risk should you account for when using Convert to TestCase on a Template?

options.text: The entire Tosca installation is removed.
All RequirementSets are deleted.
Template information is lost, so preserve it before converting back.
All browser tabs automatically close.

practiceQuiz.hint: Object-type conversion is more than changing a display label.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented reverse conversion loses the information stored in the Template.

optionExplanations.A: Conversion does not uninstall the product.
optionExplanations.B: Template conversion is unrelated to deleting RequirementSets.
optionExplanations.C: Reverse conversion loses stored template information.
optionExplanations.D: Browser-tab state is not the documented consequence.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which expression recalls the Email Test Configuration Parameter in a hypothetical login TestStep?

options.text: {CP[Email]}
@Email@
$Email$
TestConfig.Email

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the same syntax introduced back in AS1's Test Configuration Parameters lesson.
practiceQuiz.rationale: CP recalls a named configuration parameter. Resolution follows its available scope, not necessarily a project-wide value.

optionExplanations.A: CP is the supported parameter-recall command with the name in brackets.
optionExplanations.B: This placeholder is not Tosca CP recall syntax.
optionExplanations.C: Dollar-delimited text is not this parameter expression.
optionExplanations.D: This dotted property text is not the documented dynamic recall.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does Resolve Reference do to a selected reusable block reference?

options.text: It uninstalls Commander.
It makes all Library references receive this one test’s local changes.
It duplicates every Module and configuration value.
It creates locally editable steps that stop receiving that Library block’s changes, while other dependencies remain.

practiceQuiz.hint: The shared block link and technical dependencies are different.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Resolve creates an editable copy of the referenced steps; it does not copy every Module or TCP.

optionExplanations.A: Reference resolution changes the model, not installation.
optionExplanations.B: A local resolved block no longer propagates edits through that shared reference.
optionExplanations.C: Module/configuration dependencies remain rather than being universally cloned.
optionExplanations.D: The local step copy is editable independently of the Library block.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the keyboard shortcut to quickly search for and add a TestStep or Reusable TestStepBlock to a TestCase?

options.text: Ctrl+N, Ctrl+A
F9
Ctrl+J
Ctrl+T

practiceQuiz.rationale: Ctrl+T opens the 'Add TestStep' search, letting you quickly find and insert TestSteps or Reusable TestStepBlocks into a TestCase.

optionExplanations.A: This creation chord does not open Search and Add TestStep.
optionExplanations.B: F9 changes visibility rather than adding a step.
optionExplanations.C: Jump commands navigate an existing association rather than search/add.
optionExplanations.D: Ctrl+T opens the TestStep search/add dialog.

quickRecap.value: A model for concrete data-driven tests; model edits require reinstantiation of existing generated cases.
Supported shared block references need not all be resolved.
Convert the selected TestCase; reverse conversion loses template information.
Recall an available named configuration value with {CP[Name]}.
Ctrl+T opens Search and Add TestStep.
